title: Why Joash Hid in the Temple as a Child King
paragraphs: Why Joash Hid in the Temple as a Child King
There are some children in the Bible who never truly got to be children.
Before they learned how to speak clearly, they learned fear.
Before they understood crowns, they understood hiding.
Before they knew what kingship meant, they knew what it felt like to survive.
Joash was one of them.
Most people remember David facing Goliath. Most remember Moses standing before Pharaoh. Most remember Daniel in the lions’ den.
But hidden deep inside the violent shadows of Israel’s history is the story of a little boy who survived a royal massacre by being hidden inside the Temple of God.
Not because he was safe.
Because he was hunted.
And if we are honest… many people reading this know exactly what that feels like.
Not hunted by soldiers.

But hunted by trauma. By rejection. By generational darkness. By betrayal. By fear. By family wounds. By silent depression. By spiritual exhaustion. By the constant feeling that something has always tried to destroy you before your purpose could fully grow.
The story begins in 2 Kings 11 and 2 Chronicles 22.
The kingdom of Judah was bleeding spiritually. Corruption had entered the royal bloodline. Idolatry had spread like poison. And after the death of King Ahaziah, his mother Athaliah seized power.
Athaliah was not simply ambitious. She was ruthless.
Scripture says:
“When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.” — 2 Kings 11:1
The Hebrew wording here is devastating.
The phrase “destroyed all the royal offspring” comes from:
וַתְּאַבֵּד אֵת כָּל־זֶרַע הַמַּמְלָכָה (Vatte’abbed et kol-zera hammamlakhah)
The word זֶרַע (zera) means “seed,” “offspring,” or “descendants.”
This was not just political murder.
This was an attempt to erase an entire covenant bloodline.
Athaliah was trying to destroy the seed of David.
Why does that matter?
Because God had already promised David:
“Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before Me. Your throne shall be established forever.” — 2 Samuel 7:16
The Hebrew word forever here is:
עוֹלָם (olam)
It means perpetual continuity. An enduring future. A lasting covenant.
Satan has always attacked covenant seed.
Cain killed Abel. Pharaoh targeted Hebrew sons. Herod hunted babies after hearing about Jesus.
And now Athaliah tried to wipe out David’s royal descendants.
Because darkness understands something many believers forget:
What God has anointed, hell tries to kill early.
But hidden in the middle of the massacre was one small child.
Joash.
His Hebrew name is יוֹאָשׁ (Yoash).
It means: “Yahweh has given.”
Even his name carried prophetic survival.
Scripture says:
“But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being put to death…” — 2 Kings 11:2
Imagine the scene.
Screaming. Footsteps. Bodies. Panic. Blood. Treason.
And in the middle of it… somebody grabbed a child.
Not a warrior. Not a prophet. Not a general.
A child.
Some scholars believe Joash may have been less than a year old.
Too young to understand why everyone was afraid. Too young to know why he had to disappear. Too young to realize a kingdom was resting on his survival.
And yet heaven already knew.
The Bible says he was hidden in the house of the LORD for six years.
Inside the Temple.
The Hebrew phrase is:
בֵּית יְהוָה (Beit YHWH)
“The House of Yahweh.”
Think about this carefully.
The future king survived because he stayed hidden in God’s presence.
Not in political alliances. Not in military protection. Not in public visibility.
Hidden.
There is a painful truth many people spend years resisting:
Sometimes God hides you before He reveals you.
And hiding seasons often feel offensive to our flesh.
We want visibility. Recognition. Validation. Acceleration. Influence.
But heaven sometimes protects purpose through obscurity.
Joash was hidden because exposure would have killed him.
Some of you are angry because your life feels delayed.
But what if the delay protected you?
What if obscurity preserved your calling?
What if God kept certain doors closed because premature exposure would have destroyed you emotionally, spiritually, financially, or mentally?
People often complain:
“Why am I unseen?” “Why am I stuck?” “Why is my life moving slower than everyone else?”
Meanwhile heaven is whispering:
“Because you are still being protected.”
The Temple was not glamorous.
Joash spent years hidden while Athaliah ruled publicly.
Evil appeared successful.
And this is where many believers become discouraged.
Because wickedness often looks powerful temporarily.
Athaliah sat on the throne. The covenant king hid in silence.
But hidden does not mean abandoned.
Read that again.
Hidden does not mean abandoned.
Some of the holiest seasons of your life may feel invisible.
Jesus Himself spent roughly thirty years in obscurity before three years of ministry.
David was anointed long before he was enthroned. Joseph dreamed before he governed. Moses disappeared into Midian before leading Israel.
God develops depth in hidden places.
The modern world worships instant visibility. God often works through hidden formation.
And maybe this is why some people feel exhausted constantly trying to prove themselves.
Because they were never meant to build identity from public applause.
Joash survived because he stayed near the presence of God.
There are people reading this who are spiritually suffocating because you left the hiding place too early.
You traded intimacy for attention. Silence for noise. Consecration for popularity. Prayer for performance.
And now your soul feels tired.
The Temple in the Old Testament was not merely architecture. It represented God’s dwelling presence among His people.
The Hebrew word often connected to God’s dwelling glory is:
שְׁכִינָה (Shekhinah)
Though the exact noun form is not directly used in Scripture, it developed from the Hebrew root שָׁכַן (shakhan), meaning: “to dwell” “to abide” “to settle among.”
Joash was preserved where God dwelled.
And there is something deeply prophetic about that.
Because spiritually, many people are trying to survive without dwelling near God.
They consume motivation but avoid repentance. They want encouragement without surrender. They want blessing without transformation. They want resurrection power without crucifying the flesh.
But the presence of God was never meant to be decorative. It was survival.
In Greek, Jesus later says in John 15:4:
μείνατε ἐν ἐμοί (meinate en emoi)
“Abide in Me.”
The Greek word μένω (meno) means: remain, stay, continue, dwell.
Not visit occasionally. Abide.
Joash lived because he remained hidden where God dwelled.
And maybe some people are spiritually bleeding because they keep stepping away from the only place their soul can breathe.
There is another detail many overlook.
Joash was hidden by Jehosheba and protected by Jehoiada the priest.
God used faithful people to preserve the future king.
This matters deeply.
Because isolation is one of Satan’s favorite strategies.
Many believers try to survive spiritually alone.
No accountability. No discipleship. No correction. No godly covering.
But Joash survived because God surrounded him with protectors.
Not everyone around you is accidental.
Some people are assigned to help preserve your purpose.
And some relationships are literally spiritual rescue operations.
You may never fully realize how many times God used someone’s obedience to keep you alive emotionally.
A message. A prayer. A phone call. A warning. A sermon. A friend who refused to abandon you.
Some people reading this should have collapsed years ago.
But God hid you inside grace.
And eventually… the hidden king was revealed.
2 Kings 11 describes one of the most cinematic moments in Scripture.
After six years, Jehoiada brought Joash out publicly.
The child king was crowned.
Athaliah heard the celebration and rushed toward the Temple.
Scripture says:
“When she looked, there was the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom…” — 2 Kings 11:14
The rightful king had been alive the entire time.
Hidden. Preserved. Protected. Prepared.
And suddenly everything changed.
Athaliah cried:
“Treason! Treason!”
Which is deeply ironic.
Because evil often accuses righteousness of the very corruption evil committed.
But her reign ended.
The covenant line survived.
And through that preserved bloodline, generations later, Jesus Christ would enter the world.
This is why Joash matters.
His survival protected messianic prophecy.
The genealogy mattered because Jesus was called:
“The Son of David.”
In Greek:
Υἱὸς Δαβίδ (Huios David)
God was preserving redemption history through a hidden child.
Never underestimate what God is protecting when He preserves someone.
You may think your survival is random.
But heaven may see generations attached to your obedience.
There are parents reading this whose prayers are protecting children.
There are broken people reading this who survived suicide, addiction, abuse, betrayal, and despair because God still intends to use their life for His glory.
There are believers who feel forgotten when in reality they are being prepared.
And maybe that is why this story hits so hard emotionally.
Because many people know what it feels like to hide while evil seems louder.
To cry quietly. To survive silently. To wonder if God still remembers.
But Joash’s story reminds us:
God has not lost track of hidden people.

He sees the ones crying in secret. The ones rebuilding after trauma. The ones exhausted from spiritual warfare. The ones silently fighting addiction. The ones pretending to smile while battling darkness privately.
And perhaps the greatest lesson from Joash is this:
The place you thought was burying you may actually be preserving you.
Some seasons feel like confinement.
But spiritually they are protection.
Some delays feel cruel.
But spiritually they are mercy.
Some hidden years feel forgotten.
But spiritually they are preparation.
And if you are still breathing today, there is a reason.
The enemy does not attack empty destinies.
There is something hauntingly beautiful about the image of a hidden child king inside the Temple.
A small boy surrounded by chaos outside. But preserved near the presence of God.
And honestly… many believers still live there emotionally.
Trying to survive. Trying to heal. Trying to trust God while the world feels unstable.
But Scripture repeatedly shows that God specializes in preserving impossible things.
A hidden ark. A hidden prophet. A hidden Savior. A hidden kingdom. A hidden remnant. A hidden child king.
And maybe you needed this reminder today:
Just because your purpose is hidden does not mean it is dead.
Joash eventually stepped into the light.
But first… he survived the shadows.
Some of you survived things that were supposed to erase you… and heaven never stopped guarding your future.
